body:
[aida:reviewer] Head moved a FIFTH time (52e0426d33), and I went and read the live-smoke
logs instead of the check line. What I found changes the shape of TASK-1273's F1 and I
think it needs your call tonight rather than after another round.

FIRST, A CORRECTION TO MY LAST MAIL. I implied these commits were authored without a
feedback loop because the PR check line says "GitLab live forge smoke: skipping". That
was wrong. Each push gets TWO Cross-platform runs -- the push-triggered one skips the
smoke, and a dispatched one RUNS it. The smoke has run three times on this branch:

    09364e13dd  run 35571891086  live-smoke = FAILURE
    15d1668f5d  run 35572651327  live-smoke = FAILURE
    52e0426d33  run 35573642374  live-smoke = FAILURE   <- the current head, just now

So there is a loop. The problem is what the loop is being read to say.

ALL THREE DIED AT THE FIRST API CALL. I grepped each log for the test's own
"forge-smoke phase=" markers. The count is ZERO in all three. The test prints a phase
marker before every stage, so zero markers means it never got past project-create. The
15d1668f5d run finished in 11.78s; the current one is the same panic site,
forge.rs:3422.

THE CAUSE IS IN THE LOG, IN PLAIN TEXT. At 09364e13dd the old unwrap gave only:

    Result::unwrap() on an Err value: Error("expected value", line: 1, column: 1)

-- no body, undiagnosable. At 15d1668f5d and again at the current head, the new panic
carries the body, and the body is:

    stdout="<!DOCTYPE html>\n<html>\n  <head>\n    <title>Sign in - Cloudflare Access</title>

Every glab API call from the runner is being answered by a Cloudflare Access sign-in
page. That is why the create response "was not JSON". It is not asynchronous project
creation. It is that the runner cannot authenticate to gitlab.joemooney.com past
Cloudflare Access.

THIS REVALUES 15d1668f5d UPWARD AND 52e0426d33 DOWNWARD.

The "tolerate asynchronous project creation" commit is better than either of us said.
Its real contribution was DIAGNOSTIC: it turned an opaque parse error into a panic that
names the root cause on sight. It earned its place in the round.

It also proves my loop finding with a real run rather than a code read. All ten lookups
failed for the Cloudflare reason, the loop spent its ~10s, and then the panic headline
said "phase=project-create: create response was not JSON ... and project
aida-forge-live-1789975534 was not found". The headline names create-parse; the cause
is an auth wall. The body is carried so it is recoverable, but the first line points the
wrong way. That is no longer hypothetical and it goes in the verdict as you ruled.

The FIFTH commit is the one I would stop. "accept GitLab scheduled project deletion"
relaxes the assertion in phase=project-cleanup -- a phase that has never been reached in
any of the three runs. It may well be correct against a real GitLab (someone may have
hit soft-delete locally), but nothing in CI evidences it, and it cannot move the failing
run one inch. The round is now cutting commits against phases downstream of a blocker at
phase one.

WHAT THIS MEANS FOR F1. F1 asks for a green live lifecycle run at head. That cannot be
obtained by writing test code at all, at any head, until the runner can get past
Cloudflare Access -- a service token, or a bypass rule for the runner's egress. It is
infrastructure, not the spec's test. So my refusal stands, but the reason I should be
giving in the verdict is no longer "no run at this head" -- it is "three runs at three
heads, all blocked at the edge, and the blocker is not in the diff".

MY ASK. Whether TASK-1273 should keep absorbing rounds while its acceptance depends on
an auth path nobody has fixed is a disposition call, not a review one, so it is yours.
If it were mine I would tell the implementer to stop at 15d1668f5d, and split the
Cloudflare Access credential path out as its own piece of work, because otherwise the
next commit will be phase=branch-cleanup and the one after that will be lifecycle-events.

CI on the PR: Build (ubuntu-latest) still pending at the new head. I hold the formal
verdict until it is terminal.
subject: TASK-1273 F1 is blocked by CLOUDFLARE ACCESS, not test code - 3 live runs, 0 phases reached, 5th commit fixes a phase never executed
